checkpoints: After one edit, no store write occurs before 120 ms of quiet; at 120 ms the accepted text is written once.
Multiple edits within one burst reset the quiet interval and save only the latest text.
A later burst schedules and saves independently after the prior burst has completed.
An empty-string edit is saved, while editing with no current view remains a no-op.
Pending edits remain associated with the document active when each edit was accepted, including across document switches.
Opening another document, reopening the same document, closing, or disposing preserves already accepted edits and the synchronous persistence/navigation behavior that existed before coalescing.
A save that synchronously causes open or close leaves the nested navigation authoritative; an outer superseded open does not install its destination afterward.
The departing view's subscription is removed, and later status events are rendered only for the current document.
Search preview retains its existing 40 ms trailing delay and hide cancellation behavior.
Public syntax/build checks should pass after an Action; they do not establish business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not write every edit directly to the store.
Do not associate pending text with whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or discard an accepted document edit merely because its view badge is retired.
Do not allow a superseded outer open to overwrite a view installed by synchronous nested navigation.
Do not leave a retired view's store subscription active.
Do not change store event identity, text, revision, synchronous notification, or document-status filtering semantics.
Do not change createCoordinator, workspace open/edit/close/dispose, or search-preview public interfaces.
Do not alter the adjacent search preview's 40 ms timing or hide behavior.
lifecycle_identity: Each document ID identifies one reusable trailing buffer owned by the coordinator dictionary; it is independent of the current view badge.
The current view badge owns the active document ID, its document buffer, and its live subscription cleanup function.
An edit belongs to the buffer captured from the current view when edit(text) is called.
The request generation identifies whether an open operation still owns authority after callback-capable retirement and saving.
Retiring a view ends its current-view and subscription authority but does not destroy its reusable document buffer or accepted pending text.

obligations.text: createCoordinator.edit(text) must do nothing when there is no current view; otherwise it must enqueue text into that current view's document buffer instead of writing directly to the store.
Each document buffer must use trailing(env.timers, 120, ...) and write the latest accepted text to that buffer's captured document ID after 120 ms without another edit in the burst.
The same document buffer must remain reusable after a flush so subsequent bursts continue to save, while different document IDs retain independent pending state.

When replacing, closing, or disposing a view, already accepted pending text must be preserved with the editor's prior synchronous persistence behavior; retirement must flush the captured departing buffer rather than cancel or abandon it.

Before departure flushing can invoke store listeners, the departing badge must lose current ownership, its captured subscription must be detached, and its clearing presentation must be completed; this prevents nested navigation from operating on or being overwritten by the retired badge.

Because a flushed store write may synchronously navigate, open(id) must revalidate its request generation after retiring/flushing the old view and before subscribing, installing, or rendering the requested destination.

The existing trailing utility's consume ordering must remain: snapshot the pending value, retire its timer/value state, then call the consumer. This supports empty strings, prevents duplicate nested flush consumption, and permits a reentrant edit to form a later burst.
Preserve document rendering from the store, status filtering by document ID, subscription cleanup, store payload semantics, Vue disposal wiring, and all public method signatures.
Leave createSearchPreview unchanged, including its separate 40 ms trailing task and hide cancellation.

ordering_barriers: On edit: read the current view, capture its buffer, then push the supplied text into that buffer.
On trailing consumption: capture pending value, cancel/clear the ticket and pending state, then invoke the store-writing consumer.
On departure: capture the old view; clear current ownership; detach the old subscription; render the cleared document state; then flush the old buffer.

On open: increment and capture the request generation before departure; after departure and any callback-capable flush, compare the captured generation with the current generation before installing the destination.

For a retained open: acquire the destination's reusable buffer, subscribe with destination-ID filtering, install the badge, then render the document using the destination ID and the store's current text.
Store writes update the record and revision before synchronously notifying still-subscribed listeners.
preservation: Preserve createWorkspace's open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose() surface and createSearchPreview's query(text), hide() surface.
Preserve the workspace document buffer's independence from the current view badge.
Preserve synchronous store read/write/subscribe behavior and saved-event fields {id, text, revision}.
Preserve current-document status filtering and removal of the departing badge's subscription.
Preserve document rendering with the selected ID and the store value current at installation time.
Preserve close/dispose behavior, including Vue beforeDestroy calling api.dispose().
Preserve the search preview as a distinct transient trailing task with a 40 ms interval.
scope: Change only the workspace draft editor's document-edit autosave coordination and the document-buffer lifecycle needed to preserve existing navigation and persistence behavior.
Relevant public business sources are TASK, README.md, docs/host-api.md, src/coordinator.js, src/services.js, and src/Workspace.vue.
The adjacent search preview is explicitly outside the maintenance change except as behavior that must remain unchanged.

Volunteer coordination — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: coordinator dictionary

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.
Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription.
A store listener may call navigation synchronously.
All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
const resources=new Map(),bank={get(env,id){if(!resources.has(id))resources.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return resources.get(id);}};

open(id){const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;const buffer=bank.get(env,id),stop=env.store.subscribe(event=>{if(event.id===id)env.renderStatus(event);});setView({id,buffer,stop});env.renderDocument({id,text:env.store.read(id)});}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
records.set(id, text); const event = {id, text, revision: ++revision};
for (const [key, callback] of [...subscriptions]) if (subscriptions.has(key)) callback(event);
const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));
return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};
beforeDestroy(){this.api.dispose();}

triggers: Calling edit(text) while a view is current.
A second or later edit arriving before the current 120 ms timer fires.
The 120 ms timer firing after a quiet interval.
Opening another document or reopening the same document while an edit is pending.
Calling close() or dispose() while an edit is pending.
A synchronous store listener invoking workspace navigation during a timer-driven or departure-driven save.
Calling search preview query(text) or hide(), whose behavior must remain unchanged.
unknowns: The public sources do not specify exception recovery if timer operations, store writes, subscribers, or render callbacks throw.
The public sources establish synchronous navigation from store listeners, but do not establish navigation or arbitrary reentry from renderDocument, renderStatus, setView, or subscription setup.

No explicit post-disposal policy is stated for navigation initiated synchronously by a final flushed save; preservation requires accepted text and nested-navigation authority, but successor ownership beyond complete host disposal is unspecified.

The task does not state a new departure deadline explicitly; synchronous departure flushing is derived from preserving the original immediate-write persistence and fresh store reads, not from buffer ownership alone.
The public checks described in VISIBLE_CHECKS.md are syntax/build checks only and provide no stated behavioral coverage.
